exposure: Maternal age (<30 years, 30-34 years, 35-39 years, ≥40 years)
finding: The outcomes of pregnancy and childbirth for women ≥ 40 years did not vary significantly from those of younger women if pre-existing chronic diseases were managed, pregnancy-induced morbidity was monitored, regular prenatal check-ups were attended, a healthy lifestyle was maintained, and delivery occurred in a perinatal center.
mod_finding: Primiparous women ≥ 40 years had a higher overall and elective cesarean section rate compared to those younger than 30 years.
